# Lotline: Data Provenance

<!-- GENERATED by `lotline provenance --write` from the download manifest and adapter metadata.
     Do not edit by hand: change the adapter's PROVENANCE block and regenerate. -->

Every dataset Lotline uses: where it came from, which version, when it was accessed, under what license,
how it was cleaned, and its known limitations (Participant Handbook, Data and Resources). Data is downloaded
by `lotline fetch` into `LOTLINE_DATA_DIR`, never committed; each download is logged with its sha256 in
`manifest.jsonl` there, so a pull can be verified byte for byte. File counts and sizes cover each file's
latest download; entries marked superseded (`lotline manifest supersede`) are left out.

Two topics live in the hand-written companion `docs/data_availability.md`, since this file is generated: for
each state, which data are available and which Lotline used (with the reason for each gap), and the
re-identification and small-cell risk statement (what record-level data are held and what is published).

## Datasets

### Census 2020 geography: code files and DHC housing-unit parts

- **Source id:** `census_geo_codes` → table `none (inputs to eligible_parcels allocation)` (adapter `national.geoparts` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/library/reference/code-lists/ansi.html
- **Version:** 2020; publisher files last modified up to 2023-02-13
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-21
- **Files:** 586 (5.1 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Read pipe-delimited files; build 7-digit place and 10-digit county-subdivision GEOIDs
1. A place is its own county subdivision when a subdivision with its FIPS code has class C*
1. Places with more than one county get 2020 housing-unit shares by county (DHC H1_001N)
1. Places that aren't their own subdivision get 2020 housing-unit shares by township (DHC H1_001N)

**Known limitations**

- Splits use 2020 housing units, fixed for every ACS year: homes are assumed spread like 2020 housing
- Housing units of all types are used to split one-unit detached homes

### Census 2020 redistricting data (P.L. 94-171): names and total population

- **Source id:** `census_dec_pl` → table `jurisdictions` (adapter `national.decennial` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/rdo/summary-files.html
- **Version:** 2020
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 56 (0.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Short names (before the first comma) and P1_001N total population for counties, places and county subdivisions
1. Joined to the BPS jurisdiction universe by GEOID

**Known limitations**

- Jurisdictions dissolved or renamed before 2020 keep their BPS name and no population
- Unincorporated county areas get no population (county totals would overstate them)
- 2020 counts carry Census disclosure-avoidance noise for small places

### Census American Community Survey 5-year estimates (B25024, B25003, B25064, B25077, B25034)

- **Source id:** `census_acs5` → table `acs_geo_year` (adapter `national.acs` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/acs-5year.html
- **Version:** 2010–2024 (15 vintages)
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-20
- **Files:** 618 (123.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Long format: one row per geography, 5-year vintage and variable, with the published 90% MOE
1. Census special-value codes become missing; a 'controlled' MOE (-555555555) becomes 0
1. Labels kept per vintage because some categories change over time

**Known limitations**

- Adjacent 5-year vintages share four years of sample: never difference them
- 0.3-2% of estimates are suppressed, mostly small places and townships
- Requires a free Census API key (CENSUS_API_KEY); the key is never written to the manifest

### Census Building Permits Survey (BPS), annual place-level files

- **Source id:** `census_bps_place_annual` → table `bps_place_year` (adapter `national.bps` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/
- **Version:** 1992–2025 (34 vintages); publisher files last modified up to 2026-05-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 68 (57.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Parse each regional annual file; ID columns found by header name (layouts change by era)
1. Keep units and buildings for 1, 2, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings, both imputed totals and reported-only
1. Flag `imputed` when a place reported fewer than 12 months or reported units differ from the total
1. Assign GEOIDs: place, else county subdivision, else county for unincorporated/'County Part' rows; backfill earlier years by BPS ID (1992 on), then county + name, then unique name
1. Remove held-out place-years (validation/holdout.py) before the table is written

**Known limitations**

- BPS 6-digit IDs were renumbered in 1992 and reused; pre-1992 rows link by name only
- Before 2009, 0.07-2.9% of units belong to places that left the survey before FIPS codes existed and cannot be placed
- ADUs are often not recorded as new units (Upzoned #301); BPS may undercount them
- NC's BPS universe has ~157 places; most small towns' permits sit in county unincorporated totals
- Place sums exceed Census state totals in some years because Census revises state and county totals after the annual survey (BPS methodology); MN, NC, OH within 1% except 1992-93; TX 1-2% high in 2003-2014, concentrated in county unincorporated rows (e.g. Denton County 2014: +2,145 units). See reports/<st>/V0-national.md

### Census Building Permits Survey (BPS), annual state totals (reconciliation only)

- **Source id:** `census_bps_state_annual` → table `none (V0 check against bps_place_year)` (adapter `national.bps_state` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/
- **Version:** 1992–2025 (34 vintages); publisher files last modified up to 2026-05-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 34 (0.4 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Parse units for 1, 2, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings (with imputation) per state and year

**Known limitations**

- Used only to check that place files add up; never an input to the model
- Held-out state-years are not compared, so a held-out place can't be recovered by subtraction

### Census County Business Patterns: paid employment by NAICS sector (counties and U.S.)

- **Source id:** `census_cbp` → table `market_geo_year (inputs to demand_bartik, via build/demand.py)` (adapter `national.cbp` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/cbp.html
- **Version:** 2010–2023 (14 vintages)
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-20
- **Files:** 70 (5.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. 2-digit NAICS sectors; all legal forms (LFO 001) and all establishment sizes (EMPSZES 001)
1. County 999 (statewide, no fixed location) dropped; a missing county-sector row means 0 employees
1. Through 2016, suppressed cells (EMP 0 with a flag a-m) are set inside the flag's range at suppressed_cell_position (config/params/demand.yaml) and marked imputed

**Known limitations**

- Private non-farm wage employment only: no government, self-employed or most farm jobs
- March employment each year; county is where the establishment is, not where workers live
- From 2017 CBP adds noise to every cell instead of suppressing; small cells can be off by 5% or more
- Requires a free Census API key (CENSUS_API_KEY); the key is never written to the manifest

### Census TIGERweb boundaries, ACS 2025 vintage (incorporated places, county subdivisions)

- **Source id:** `census_tigerweb_acs2025` → table `none (boundaries for point assignment)` (adapter `national.tiger_boundaries` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/tigerwebmain/TIGERweb_main.html
- **Version:** acs2025
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-20
- **Files:** 140 (118.4 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Query layers 18 (incorporated places) and 15 (county subdivisions) of the ACS 2025 group by state
1. Keep GEOID (7-digit place, 10-digit county subdivision), NAME, FUNCSTAT and polygon rings in WGS84
1. Points are assigned with the even-odd rule over every ring, so holes and enclaves are respected

**Known limitations**

- One boundary vintage (January 2025) is applied to every year: annexations move points near edges
- Census-designated places are excluded on purpose: they are statistical areas, not permit issuers
- A point exactly on a boundary goes to one side by a fixed rule, not by any legal determination

### City of Austin Issued Construction Permits (Development Services, daily)

- **Source id:** `austin_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.tx.austin_permits` v1.1)
- **Source:** https://data.austintexas.gov/Building-and-Development/Issued-Construction-Permits/3syk-w9eu
- **Version:** 2026-10-18, 2026-10-19; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-18
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-19
- **Files:** 7 (98.0 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public Domain U.S. Government (City of Austin open data)
- **Required attribution:** City of Austin, Texas - data.austintexas.gov

**Cleaning steps**

1. Socrata pager with an explicit field list: no contractor or applicant names, organizations, phones or addresses, no property address, legal description or portal link. The work description is downloaded (raw pages only) for the description fallback and never stored in the table
1. Server-side filter: building permits (permittype BP) whose permit_class carries a Census code 101-106, 436 or 645-649 (R- or C- prefix), plus plain-class 'Residential'/'Commercial' permits with work class 'New'
1. Rows without an issue date, issued before 1970, or with status VOID, Withdrawn, Aborted or Cancelled... are dropped (never validly issued); Expired permits are kept, as in the BPS
1. jurisdiction 'AUSTIN FULL PURPOSE' or 'AUSTIN LTD' (limited purpose) → Austin city 4805000; every other value (Austin ETJ, other cities, SB 2038 ETJ releases, blank) is left out
1. building_type_std from the Census code: 101 SFD, 102 ADU (the city's 'Secondary Apartment' class, which its ADU dataset 687g-qcqy names as the ADU class), 103 U2, 104 U3_4, 105 MF5, 106 mixed use and 436 additions → OTHER; plain classes from the description, else UNKNOWN
1. Units: housing_units kept where it fits the code (101/102 → 1; 103 → 1 or 2, since duplexes are permitted per side or per building; 104 → 3-4; 105 → 5+; 106 → 1+); otherwise 101/102 → 1 and 103 → 2 (derived); 104/105/106 from the description (inferred) or null
1. Demolitions 645-649: is_demolition, units_new 0, units_removed from housing_units where it fits the code, else 645 → 1, 646 → 2 (derived); 647/648 without a plausible count and 649 unknown
1. 436 'Addition to increase housing units': is_conversion, units_new from the description (inferred) or null (housing_units there counts the building's units, not units added)
1. adu_type of 102 permits from the description (attached/detached/internal conversion), else unknown
1. reform_flag_raw: 'TWO UNIT RES' / 'THREE UNIT RES' when the description names the HOME two- or three-unit residential use
1. final_date = completed_date (final_date_type completion); application_date = applieddate
1. parcel_id = '48453' + tcad_id where it is a Travis CAD geographic ID (digits only); an ID that starts with a letter (e.g. 'R654373', the account format of the Williamson and Hays appraisal districts) is kept as written, without a county prefix, because the permit doesn't say which district it is
1. permit_class_raw = permit_class | work_class; Holdout filter applied (Texas has no holdouts)
1. Cross-check only (not loaded): the city's ADU dataset 687g-qcqy (a view of R-102 permits) was read once under this source as 'adu_permits_687g' (permit number, class, date, status, jurisdiction, units); all 3,244 of its permits are R-102 rows of 3syk-w9eu (2026-10-18)

**Known limitations**

- The jurisdiction attribute reflects current boundaries, so permits issued before an annexation are assigned by today's city limits
- Austin full- and limited-purpose areas both count as Austin (the city zones and permits both); the Census place boundary may not include limited-purpose areas
- R-102 (ADU) nearly stops after HOME (2024): two- and three-unit uses are one permit per building (each home an R-101 or R-103), marked only by the description phrase, so ADU series break in 2024
- Five-or-more permits sometimes repeat a project total on each building permit (e.g. nine permits on one parcel in 2022 each report 280 units), so 2019-2023 5+ units exceed the BPS (up to 1.41x in 2022); kept as reported here and counted once when permits are counted (D-008)
- Single-family (R-101) units alone run 5-20% below BPS 1-unit units 2010-2025: the BPS files most ADUs and duplex sides as 1-unit homes. All homes in 1-2 unit buildings (R-101 + R-102 + R-103 vs BPS 1 + 2 units) are within 10% every year (0.91-1.09; reports/tx/V0.md)
- Mixed-use (106) dwellings are OTHER, not MF5: compare 5+ counts with the BPS with and without them
- Some 104/105 permits lack a plausible housing_units value; their units come from the description or stay null
- Records are revised in place (status, completion); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### City of Cincinnati Building Permits (BLDS, 2010 to present) and combo permits with plan review

- **Source id:** `cincy_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.oh.cincy_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/Thriving-Healthy-Neighborhoods/Cincinnati-Building-Permits/uhjb-xac9
- **Version:** 2026-10-18; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-18
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-18
- **Files:** 4 (4.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public Domain (City of Cincinnati open data)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Selected fields exclude company names, addresses and links; from the combo dataset only the permit number, sub-type and work description are requested (never reviewer names or review comments)
1. Server-side filter: Building permits with work class RNEW/CNEW, Wrecking permits RDMO/CDMO; trade permits (plumbing, HVAC, excavation/fill) for the same projects are not downloaded
1. Combo permits: only rows whose work description names an ADU, carriage house, garage apartment, in-law suite or townhouse; parsed with lotline.parse.permit_text, text never stored; those permit numbers are also downloaded from the main dataset whatever their work class
1. Permits never issued, withdrawn, voided, revoked, denied or refunded are dropped
1. building_type_std from the building-code use group and units: 1-2-3 family/R-3/R-5/R-2 by units (1 SFD inferred, 2 U2, 3-4 U3_4, 5+ MF5); other use groups OTHER with unknown units; 0 or blank units → unknown; the combo description turns a permit into ADU (1 unit) or TH, marked inferred
1. Wrecking permits: is_demolition, units_new 0, units_removed = units for dwelling use groups
1. final_date = coissueddate (certificate of occupancy)
1. Every row is assigned to Cincinnati (3915000), the permit-issuing city
1. Holdout filter applied (Ohio has no holdouts)

**Known limitations**

- No Census building-type code: 1-unit permits can't be split into detached and attached houses except where the combo description says townhouse; they are SFD, inferred
- Apartments inside mixed-use or commercial use groups (B, M, ...) are OTHER with unknown units
- ADUs are found only where the combo work description names one; an ADU described otherwise is missed
- units on wrecking permits is the building's units; commercial-use wrecking permits have unknown units removed
- The city revises records in place; each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### City of Columbus Building Permits (Building & Zoning Services, nightly, 2010 to present)

- **Source id:** `columbus_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.oh.columbus_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=f7a785b863454d96a0fe3f5aa5368e7d
- **Version:** 2026-10-23, 2026-10-30; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-30
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-30
- **Files:** 18 (14.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC0-1.0 (City of Columbus open data)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude applicant and business names, site address, ZIP and permit-portal links (no personal data); the layer has no free-text description field
1. Server-side filter keeps only new-structure and demolition permits: GENERAL_TYPE '... - New Structure' or '... - Demolition', or CONST_TYPE_CODE 645-649 (29,183 of about 685,000 permits on 2026-10-15); trade, partial (foundation-only, advance-start), repair and alteration permits are not downloaded because they repeat the project's Census code and unit count
1. Permits without an issued date, and voided or withdrawn applications (B1_APPL_STATUS 'VOID ...', 'Void ...', 'Withdrawn'), are dropped; expired permits are kept (BPS counts permits when issued)
1. building_type_std from the Census BPS code in CONST_TYPE_CODE (101 SFD, 102 TH, 103 U2, 104 U3_4, 105 MF5, 106 manufactured → OTHER); 3xx/4xx codes (nonresidential, additions, alterations) → OTHER with unknown units; a missing code → UNKNOWN
1. Units: UNITS is kept only where it fits the code (1 for SFD/manufactured, 1+ for townhouse, 2 for duplex, 3-4 for 104, 5+ for 105); otherwise SFD/TH/manufactured → 1 and duplex → 2 (units_confidence=derived); 104 and 105 without a plausible count stay null
1. Demolitions (645-649 or a Demolition permit type): is_demolition, units_new 0, units_removed from UNITS where it fits the code, else 645 → 1, 646 → 2; 649 and nonresidential demolitions unknown
1. final_date is LAST_STATUS_DT when the status is 'Certificate of Occupancy Issued' or 'Final Inspection Approved' (a proxy: the date of the last status change)
1. ADUs: permit numbers flagged by franklin_permits.adu_flags (Franklin County Auditor permit file, work descriptions) are also downloaded; a match on permit number (and parcel, for all-digit numbers) that is not an MEP permit becomes ADU (1 unit, inferred, adu_type from the flag)
1. CONST_TYPE_CODE and GENERAL_TYPE copied to permit_class_raw
1. Every row is assigned to Columbus (3918000), the permit-issuing city
1. Holdout filter applied (Ohio has no holdouts; called for uniformity)

**Known limitations**

- ADUs are known only where the auditor's file has the permit and its description names the ADU (franklin_permits rules); flags under legacy permit numbers that the layer lacks (2015) are not added, so ADU counts before 2016 are low
- Five-or-more and three-or-four family permits without a plausible UNITS value have unknown units (null), not zero
- Nonresidential new buildings (3xx codes) often carry a UNITS value (e.g. mixed-use or hotel rooms); these are not counted as dwellings, matching the BPS, which classifies a building by its main use
- Conversions that add units inside existing buildings are not visible: alteration permits outside the filter are not downloaded, and 434 (residential additions/alterations) permits that fall inside it are OTHER with unknown units, because UNITS there holds the building's units, not units added
- final_date is the last status-change date, not a dated CO field
- UNITS is sometimes the whole project's count repeated on each building's permit (e.g. nine 2023 permits on one parcel each report the same 198-unit total) or a typo (a 2012 townhouse permit with 433 units on 2,274 sq ft); these are kept as reported, so single years can exceed the Census BPS
- Pre-2010 permits are in separate 'Historic Building Permits' services, not loaded
- The city revises records in place (status changes); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### City of Columbus Council variance ordinances (Legistar Web API)

- **Source id:** `columbus_legistar` → table `permits` (adapter `states.oh.columbus_variances` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://columbus.legistar.com/Legislation.aspx
- **Version:** 2026-10-30
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-30
- **Files:** 2 (1.0 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** City of Columbus public legislative records (Legistar Web API; no reuse terms stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Every ordinance with 'Variance' in its title (substringof('Variance',MatterTitle) and MatterTypeName eq 'Ordinance'), paged 1000 at a time; only the id, file number, title, passed date and status are requested
1. ADU approvals only, from named rules on the title's purpose clause (carriage or coach house, ADU, a dwelling above a garage, a second dwelling, two single-unit dwellings on one lot, a rear dwelling, habitable space above a detached garage)
1. Dropped: not passed or later repealed; conforming an existing dwelling only; commercial, manufacturing or institutional districts; multi-unit buildings; dwellings on two or more lots
1. One row per variance number (CV..), dated by the ordinance's passed date; titles are read in memory and never stored
1. Holdout filter applied (Ohio has no holdouts)

**Known limitations**

- Approvals, not construction: the city reports 110 variances approved against 57 ADU permits for 2019 to Sep 2025, so counts here are an upper bound on new ADUs
- Council approval precedes the building permit by months; the year can differ from the permit's
- 'Habitable space above a detached garage' is counted (recall over precision) although some are studios or offices; its rows are labelled in permit_class_raw
- No parcel: the title's address is not matched, so a variance and the later permit for the same ADU are not linked (observed_adu_counts keeps the larger source per year, never the sum)
- Ends with Ord. 2526-2025 (effective 2025-12-24): ADUs need no variance after that

### City of Dallas building permits 1971-2024 (POSSE extract, Planning and Development)

- **Accessed:** 2026-10-23
- **Files:** 74 (58.9 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested: building permits for new construction and additions that are single-family, multifamily or have a dwelling land use
1. Requested fields exclude the address, ZIP code, coordinates and comments; the work description is read only by the description parser and never kept
1. Kept: status Complete, Issued or Expired with an issue date; one row per permit number

### City of Fort Worth development permits (Accela, since 2001)

- **Source id:** `fw_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.tx.fw_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://data.fortworthtexas.gov/
- **Version:** 2026-10-23; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-23
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-23
- **Files:** 331 (125.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC-BY 4.0 (City of Fort Worth open data)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested: residential building and accessory-structure permits, and commercial building permits with a residential use; trade, backflow, forestry, grading, design-review and non-residential commercial permits are not
1. Requested fields exclude owner names, site addresses, legal descriptions and coordinates; the work description is read only by the description parser and never kept
1. Status snapshots collapsed to one row per Permit_No (units counted once, D-008); kept if any row is Issued / Issued Without Contractor / Finaled or the latest status is Expired
1. issue_year = filing year (no issue date in the source; date_precision year); application_date = File_Date; final_date = date of the Finaled status
1. building_type_std and units from the use (config/crosswalks/tx_fw_use.csv); Units when it fits the type (reported), else the type's count (derived); apartment buildings only from a Units of 2 or more; Units above 1,000 read as missing
1. ADU when the description parser names one on a residential building or accessory-structure permit (inferred)
1. jurisdiction_geoid = Fort Worth (4827000) for every row; valuation_usd = JobValue; floor_area_sqft = SqFt

**Known limitations**

- No issue date: permits are dated by filing year, a few weeks before issue
- Demolition permits are not in the table: units_removed is mostly missing
- ADUs only where the description names one ('ADU', 'accessory dwelling'); the source's 'Accessory Dwelling' use also holds storm shelters and game rooms and is not used on its own. Fort Worth allows accessory dwellings in one-family districts only when not rented (TX-4827000-adu-2010), so these are non-rental units
- No parcel number; permits cannot be joined to parcels
- Duplex permits with Units 1 are read as one permit per half of the building
- 5+ unit homes run above BPS in some years (2.6x in 2020, 2023 and 2024): some projects repeat the project total on every building's permit, and with no parcel number the D-008 rule cannot group them (issue #221); 2022's excess (1.8x) has another cause, not yet found

### City of Minneapolis Assessing Department parcel data (assessment years 2017-2026)

- **Source id:** `mpls_assessor_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `states.mn.mpls_assessor_parcels` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=d9bb827c0465472a937d325b22f9939d
- **Version:** asmt_2017, asmt_2018, asmt_2019, asmt_2020, asmt_2021, asmt_2022, asmt_2023, asmt_2024, asmt_2025, asmt_2026; publisher files last modified up to 2026-08-10
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-20
- **Files:** 1065 (403.6 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC0 1.0 (City of Minneapolis open data waiver)
- **Required attribution:** City of Minneapolis Assessing Department (open data, CC0)

**Cleaning steps**

1. One table per assessment year (https://services.arcgis.com/afSMGVsC7QlRK1kZ/arcgis/rest/services/Assessors_Parcel_Data_2017 ... Assessing_Department_Parcel_Data_2026), downloaded with the ArcGIS pager, requesting only the PIN, assessment year, zoning, parcel area, property type, land and building value, homestead, building use, year built, above-ground area and total units (names differ by layout). Owner, taxpayer and address fields are never requested
1. vintage = assessment year; vintage_date = January 2 of that year (the assessment date the city states)
1. parcel_id = '27053' (Hennepin) + the 13-digit PIN (a leading 'p' and punctuation removed); the 2025-2026 tables list one row per building: units and above-ground area are summed per PIN, year built is the earliest, building use is the building with the most units
1. jurisdiction_geoid = 2743000 (Minneapolis); holdout filter applied with the snapshot rule
1. land_use_std: property type by config/crosswalks/mn_land_use_mpls.csv, overridden for residential parcels by building use (config/crosswalks/mn_land_use_mpls_building.csv); flagged rules refined by TOTAL_UNITS; land_use_raw = property type | building use
1. units = TOTAL_UNITS where > 0; a 0 is kept only on non-residential or vacant parcels (the 2025-2026 tables report 0 for single-family houses), else null
1. lot_sqft = parcel area; year_built 1800 to the roll year + 1; bldg_sqft = above-ground area (> 0)
1. land_value / bldg_value = the assessor's values as of January 2 (value_basis=market); homestead from HOMESTEADED / Y
1. zoning_raw = ZONING, zoning_source = 'assessor'

**Known limitations**

- Minneapolis only; no sale prices; coordinates are in the county system and are not converted
- Layouts and labels change over time (property types were renamed in 2025); land use is rule-based
- TOTAL_UNITS is 0 for single-family houses in 2025-2026, so those units are null
- Assessment-date tables, not year-end rolls: the 2024 table describes parcels on 2024-01-02

### City of Minneapolis CCS Permits (building permits, Dec 2016 on)

- **Source id:** `mpls_ccs_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.mn.mpls_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://opendata.minneapolismn.gov/datasets/cityoflakes::ccs-permits
- **Version:** 2026-10-14; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 80 (72.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC0 1.0 (City of Minneapolis open data waiver); CC0 1.0 (City of Minneapolis waives copyright in its open data)
- **Required attribution:** City of Minneapolis, Construction Code Services (open data, CC0)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download the CCS_Permits feature layer (https://services.arcgis.com/afSMGVsC7QlRK1kZ/arcgis/rest/services/CCS_Permits/FeatureServer/0) with the ArcGIS pager into a dated snapshot (the layer is a rolling window from Dec 2016), requesting only OBJECTID, APN, permitNumber, permitType, occupancyType, workType, status, dwellingUnitsNew, dwellingUnitsEliminated, permit_Value, totalFees, issueDate, completeDate, comments where permitType IN ('Res','Commercial','Wrecking'). Applicant name, owner name and applicant address/city are never requested; Plumbing, Mechanical and Site permits are not downloaded
1. One row per permitNumber: a permit listed once per parcel it touches (about 3,700 permits) is collapsed to its lowest OBJECTID row, and its unit counts are counted once, not once per parcel
1. parcel_id: '27053' (Hennepin) + the 13-digit APN; for a multi-parcel permit, the lowest APN
1. issueDate / completeDate (epoch ms, UTC) → local Minneapolis calendar dates; issue_year from issue_date; date_precision=day
1. final_date = completeDate only for Closed permits, final_date_type=final_inspection (the item description defines completeDate as the passed final inspection); cancelled permits get no final_date
1. dwellingUnitsNew / dwellingUnitsEliminated (text) → units_new / units_removed; empty → null (unknown), never 0; units_confidence=reported when both are present
1. Wrecking permits: is_demolition=True; dwellingUnitsEliminated is always empty there, so a whole SFD wrecked → units_removed=1 (derived), any other building → null
1. building_type_std from occupancyType: SFD→SFD, TH→TH, TFD (two- or three-family)→DTQ, 3to4→U3_4, MFD→MF5, Comm and Accessory→OTHER, blank→UNKNOWN; when TFD/3to4/MFD/Mixed/Comm reports N≥2 new units the Census size class of N is used (2→U2, 3-4→U3_4, 5-6→U5_6, 7+→U7P)
1. ADU (type_confidence=inferred): Res permit on an SFD/TFD/Accessory occupancy; work type Accessory, Conversion, UnitCon, Remodel, Addition, UnitFinish, or New on an Accessory structure; comments name an ADU and do not negate it ('NOT AN ADU', 'FUTURE ADU') or describe work on an existing ADU (unless legalizing it); an existing house on the parcel (the occupancy is a house and the work is not a new house, the comments say 'accessory to a SFD'/'existing house', or the APN has another non-new house permit); and at most 1 new unit reported. adu_type from the comments (basement/attic → internal_conversion, garage/detached → detached, attached/addition → attached, else unknown)
1. ADU units: a permit typed ADU that reports 0 or no new units gets units_new=1, inferred (an ADU permit adds a home)
1. A new SFD/two-family permit whose comments name an ADU gets a second row (permit_id + '-ADU', 1 unit, inferred, no valuation/fees); if the house reports the ADU in its units (SFD 2+, two-family 3+), one unit moves to the ADU row (house row 'derived')
1. is_conversion=True for work types Conversion/UnitCon or when a permit both adds and removes units
1. valuation_usd = permit_Value, fees_paid_usd = totalFees (city fees and taxes; 0 kept as 0)
1. permit_class_raw = permitType:occupancyType:workType:status (status is kept so cancelled permits can be dropped downstream)
1. comments are read for the ADU rule only and never stored
1. jurisdiction_geoid = 2743000 (Minneapolis); held-out place-years removed (validation/holdout.py)

**Known limitations**

- Rolling window: the layer starts in Dec 2016 and older permits drop out; only dated snapshots keep them. 2016 holds December only
- dwellingUnitsNew is 0 on most ADU permits; ADU units are therefore inferred (1 per ADU permit), not reported
- ADU typing is inferred from free text: it misses ADUs whose scope of work doesn't say 'ADU'
- Cancelled, expired and withdrawn permits stay in the table (status is in permit_class_raw)
- Demolished units are unknown for anything but whole single-family houses
- A permit listed on several parcels keeps only its lowest APN
- Minneapolis only; Commercial permits cover apartments, mixed use and non-residential alike

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude owner, contractor, address, coordinate and comment fields (no personal data)
1. Permits without an issued date (applications under review) are dropped; issue_year is the issue date's year
1. building_type_std from the Census BPS code in censuslandusecode (101 SFD, 102 TH, 103 U2, 104 U3_4, 105 MF5, 112 manufactured → OTHER); adu_type Attached/Detached/Internal ADU → ADU
1. Units repair: housingunitstotal is kept only where it fits the type code (1 for SFD/ADU/manufactured, 1+ for townhouse, 2 for duplex, 3-4 for 104, 5+ for 105; 0 never fits); otherwise SFD/TH/ADU/manufactured → 1 and duplex → 2 with units_confidence=derived; 104 and 105 without a plausible count stay null
1. Alterations, additions, accessory and nonresidential permits: units_new null (their housingunitstotal is the existing building's units, not new ones)
1. Demolitions (645-649): is_demolition, units_new 0, units_removed from housingunitsexist or the code (645 → 1, 646 → 2)
1. missing_middle flag copied to reform_flag_raw; censuslandusecode/workclass to permit_class_raw
1. Every row is assigned to Raleigh (3755000), the permit-issuing office, including permits issued in its extraterritorial jurisdiction (totals match the Census BPS Raleigh row within a few %)
1. Description fallback (lotline.parse.permit_text): where units or type stay unknown, the work description (proposedworkdescription) fills only that value, marked inferred: 104/105 counts that fit the code, units removed by demolitions, and the type of permits with no code; never overrides a reported or derived value; the parser's building_units is not stored
1. Holdout filter applied (NC holdout is Charlotte; no Raleigh rows are held out)

**Known limitations**

- housingunitstotal is nearly empty for permits issued from 2024 on, so most 2024+ unit counts are derived from the building-type code rather than reported
- Five-or-more and three-or-four family permits without a plausible reported count have unknown units (null). From 2024 almost every 105 permit is unknown, so 2024+ multifamily units are missing, not zero; the description parser recovers a count only where the text states one plainly (it is truncated at 100 characters, and project totals or two different counts give no count)
- Townhouse permits with no reported count are derived as 1 unit; the few that cover a whole building (4-9 units reported in 2023-24) would be undercounted when unreported
- The adu_type and missing_middle flags are populated only from 2019-2020 on; earlier ADUs and missing-middle projects are not flagged
- The catalog's '2013 anomaly' was not reproduced: 2013 new-dwelling counts match the Census BPS; implausible values are scattered (mostly duplexes reported as 1 unit before 2008) and repaired
- Alterations, additions and accessory structures are kept as OTHER with unknown units; an internal conversion that adds a unit is visible only when flagged as an ADU
- The city revises records in place (status, CO dates); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### City of Saint Paul Building Permits (mid-2015 to mid-2025)

- **Source id:** `stpaul_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.mn.stpaul_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=cb618c6b5f8f46b696674e74a3fb5b2d
- **Version:** 2026-10-19; publisher files last modified up to 2025-07-01
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19
- **Files:** 45 (41.3 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain
- **Required attribution:** City of Saint Paul, Department of Safety and Inspections (open data)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download the Building_Permits_ feature layer (https://services1.arcgis.com/9meaaHE3uiba0zr8/arcgis/rest/services/Building_Permits_/FeatureServer/0) with the ArcGIS pager into a dated snapshot, requesting only OBJECTID, PERMITNUMBER, PIN, STATUS, ISSUEDATE, EXPIRATIONDATE, FINALDATE, FOLDER_TYPE, SUB_TYPE, WORK_TYPE, FOLDERDESCRIPTION, EST_VALUE_OF_WORK, STATE_VALUATION, LATITUE, LONGITUTE. Street address, contractor name and contractor address are never requested; the work description is kept in the raw snapshot only
1. ISSUEDATE / FINALDATE (epoch ms, UTC) → local St. Paul calendar dates; issue_year from issue_date; date_precision=day; permits never issued are dropped
1. Held-out place-years removed (validation/holdout.py: V5-MN-STPAUL hides 2024-2026) right after the dates are read, before any other step
1. permit_id: 'stp-' + PERMITNUMBER; parcel_id: '27123' (Ramsey) + the 12-digit PIN, else null
1. building_type_std from SUB_TYPE: Single Family Dwelling→SFD, 2-Family/Duplex→U2, Accessory Structure, Commercial and Institutional→OTHER, Residential (Multi-Fam) and Mixed→UNKNOWN
1. Units (derived): a New single-family permit adds 1, a New duplex 2; Repair and Express Repair add and remove 0; everything else null (unknown)
1. final_date = FINALDATE for Finaled permits, final_date_type=final_inspection
1. valuation_usd = STATE_VALUATION (the building valuation the permit fee is set on)
1. permit_class_raw = SUB_TYPE:WORK_TYPE:STATUS

**Known limitations**

- No unit counts and no ADU flag: units are known only for new single-family houses and duplexes; use Met Council permits for St. Paul outcomes
- Rolling 10-year window: permits issued before 2015-06-30 had already dropped out at the first snapshot (2026-10-19); the layer was last edited on 2025-07-01 (layer metadata)
- No demolition or wrecking permits in the layer
- Multifamily and mixed-use permits can't be sized (UNKNOWN), so DTQ vs MF5 can't be told apart here
- St. Paul permits from 2024 on are held out (V5 blind test) and absent from the table
- About 1% of pre-2024 permits have no PIN

### City of San Antonio building permits issued (Development Services, since 2020-07)

- **Source id:** `sa_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.tx.sa_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://data.sanantonio.gov/dataset/building-permits
- **Version:** 2026-10-23; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-18
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-23
- **Files:** 2 (106.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC-BY (City of San Antonio open data, Creative Commons Attribution)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Two CSVs (2020-2024 and 2025 on) from the /dataset/ download links; the CKAN API and DataStore, disallowed by robots.txt, are never used
1. The primary contact, location and coordinates are never read; the address (ETJ test) and project name (description parser) are read in memory and never kept
1. Kept: new residential and commercial buildings, ADUs, residential accessory buildings and additions, residential foundations, demolitions; one row per permit number (earliest submitted revision)
1. ADU = 'Res Accessory Dwelling Permit' (1 unit, derived); new residential building = SFD 1 unit (derived) unless the parser reads another type; accessory, addition and foundation permits 0 units; new commercial buildings and demolitions from the parser, else unknown
1. Permits in the ETJ (address 'City of San Antonio ETJ' or council district 0) filed under the Bexar County remainder (48029), the rest under San Antonio (4865000)
1. issue_date = DATE ISSUED; application_date = DATE SUBMITTED; valuation_usd = DECLARED VALUATION; floor_area_sqft = AREA (SF)

**Known limitations**

- Starts 2020-07-20 (Accela); 2020 is a part year
- No unit count: new residential buildings are counted as one house each unless the project name says otherwise, and apartments only where the project name gives a count; use BPS for 2-4 and 5+ units
- ETJ permits are all filed under Bexar County although parts of the ETJ lie in neighbouring counties; BPS counts them under San Antonio
- No completion date and no parcel number

### City-County of Durham All Building Permits (hosted ArcGIS layer, daily, Oct 2007 to present)

- **Source id:** `durham_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.nc.durham_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=c169c12616a54fcc99aac37ff4997a82
- **Version:** 2026-10-21; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-21
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-21
- **Files:** 51 (38.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** City of Durham open data (Privacy Notice and Terms of Service on the Durham Open Data Hub)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude owner, contractor, address, project-name, comment and description fields (PROJECT_TYPE and COMMENTS hold phone numbers and e-mail addresses)
1. Kept: permits with an ISSUE_DATE whose PmtStatus is not Void, Disapproved or Received
1. building_type_std from BLD_Type (Single Family House SFD, Townhouse TH, Accessory Dwelling ADU, Duplex U2, 3-4 Residential Units U3_4, 5+ Residential Units MF5, Mobile Home OTHER; Modular Unit with Single Family occupancy SFD inferred); a multifamily label contradicted by a reported count of 2+ is re-typed by the count (type_confidence inferred)
1. Units only for new construction (BLDB_ACTIVITY NEW): DWELLING_UNITS kept where it fits the type (1 SFD/ADU/mobile home, 1+ TH, 1-2 duplex, 3-4, 5+), else SFD/TH/ADU/mobile home → 1 derived, multifamily → null
1. Demolitions: units_new 0, units_removed from DWELLING_UNITS or the type (SFD/TH/ADU/mobile 1, duplex 2)
1. final_date = CO_SIGNOFF_DATE (certificate of occupancy); parcel_id = PIN15 as published
1. Jurisdiction by location: permit point inside the City of Durham corporate limits (CoD_Boundary layer, fetched with the permits) → 3719000, outside → 37063; permits without a point take the majority side of located permits sharing the longest 8-5 digit prefix of their NC PIN, then of their parent parcel (pending plats); the rest (~0.5%) go to the city
1. Annexation date (#94): a located city permit inside an approved Consolidated Annexation case (Planning layer 19) approved after its issue date goes to the county (37063)
1. One row per permit number (a permit spanning several parcels is listed once per parcel)
1. Permits whose side can't be inferred (~0.5%) default to the city (Ben, 2026-10-14): ~92% of located permits are in the city
1. reform_flag_raw: 'EHC' plus whitelisted components (adu, duplex, flag_lot, small_lot) for permits whose PROJECT_TYPE starts 'EHC', fetched by a server-side filter; the text is never stored
1. Holdout filter applied (NC holdout is Charlotte; no Durham rows are held out)

**Known limitations**

- City limits are today's, corrected by annexation date from 2013 on only: annexations approved before 2013 are not in the Consolidated Annexation layer, so a 2007-2012 permit on land annexed in 2007-2012 still counts as city; permits placed by PIN are not re-dated
- About 3% of permits have no point; their side is inferred from neighbouring PINs (97-99.5% agreement on located permits) and ~0.5% are assigned to the city by default
- 5+ and 3-4 unit permits without a plausible DWELLING_UNITS have unknown units (null)
- Mixed-use and other Non-Residential buildings with apartments are OTHER with unknown units: their DWELLING_UNITS mixes in hotels, parking decks and project totals
- ADU permits filed as alterations, additions or other work (about 110) have unknown units: the permit may create the ADU or alter an existing one
- Duplex sides are often permitted separately (1 unit each), so permit counts exceed BPS building counts for duplexes
- The city revises records in place (status, CO dates); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

**Cleaning steps**

1. Skip FHFA's title rows; keep native HPI, HPI with 2000 base, and annual change
1. Prefix geography codes by level (county:27053, zip5:55415, ...)

### Franklin County Auditor permit file (Outside User Files, appraisal snapshots)

- **Source id:** `franklin_auditor` → table `permits` (adapter `research.ws_oh_adu_scan` v0)
- **Source:** https://auditor.franklincountyohio.gov/Auditor/FTP
- **Version:** 2016-03-15, 2016-12-22, 2017-12-19, 2018-12-17, 2019-12-18, 2020-12-25, 2021-12-22, 2022-12-15, 2022-12-20, 2023-12-26, 2024-12-30, 2025-12-31, 2026-10-15; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-15
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-27
- **Files:** 15 (553.2 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Franklin County Auditor public records (disclaimer: 'as is'; no reuse terms stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Snapshots 2022-12-15, 2026-10-15 read together (1990 to the present); a permit repeated across snapshots or parcels is kept once per permit number and taxing district
1. Rows without a permit number (auditor field notes) or with an impossible date are dropped
1. ADU permits only, from named description rules favouring recall (ADU noun + creation verb; a carriage house described as a garage needs living space; work on existing units, repair and trade permit numbers and multi-unit buildings excluded); trade permits mark the new-building or addition permit they cite, flagged from the earliest trade permit when the project permit is not in the file; one ADU per parcel in any two years
1. Parcel matched to oh_parcels for the jurisdiction; parcels not in the roll take their taxing district's jurisdiction where ≥95% of its parcels lie in one
1. Columbus permits are not written here: columbus_permits relabels its own matching permits as ADUs
1. Work descriptions are read in memory and never stored
1. Holdout filter applied (Ohio has no holdouts)

**Known limitations**

- Only permits the issuing office reports to the auditor; not a complete record of new houses, so only ADU permits are kept
- ADU flags are read from free text (inferred) and favour recall: an ADU described without one of the named nouns is missed, and some flagged carriage houses or in-law suites may be garages or rooms
- No permit status: a flagged ADU may have been withdrawn or never built
- Issue date is the auditor's permit date (PERMDT), which may be the application or issue date depending on the office
- A jurisdiction with no ADU permit has no row

### Mecklenburg County Building Permit Locations (Code Enforcement, since 1990)

- **Source id:** `meck_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `manual_export` v1)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=fc9d171ecd4d44a58c7dad840cd58aa2
- **Version:** 2026-10-12
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-21
- **Files:** 1 (73.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Mecklenburg County GIS public data (accuracy disclaimer; no license stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Read from Ben's hand download of the county's 'Building Permits - Winchester' GeoPackage (Open Data Viewer, data dated 2026-10-12, registered 2026-10-21; downloaded from Europe through a US VPN because the county's GIS servers did not answer there); the server query is used only when no file is registered
1. Holdout-first filter in the query itself (file_where in SQLite; server_where on the live layer): only permits issued before the Charlotte window (2023-06-01, from the holdout config), or later in a non-held-out town by taxjuris; held-out rows are never read
1. holdout.apply on the point-based place right after the rows are built (D-012: 3712000 and 37119)
1. Requested fields exclude owner name, phone, e-mail, address, city, state and ZIP, project name, number, description and address; permitdesc/workdesc are read only by the description parser and never kept
1. File points (x_coord/y_coord, NC State Plane feet, EPSG:2264) converted to lon/lat by stateplane.to_lonlat (checked: median 7 m from the pre-UDO parcel centroids of the same parcels)
1. jurisdiction_geoid = place of the permit point (TIGERweb ACS 2025), else taxjuris, else 37119
1. building_type_std and units from the Census item code in usdcdesc (config/crosswalks/nc_meck_usdc_codes.csv, including the county's own 102 townhouse, 112 mobile home, 114 and 115 condominium codes); numunits when it fits the type; description parser for gaps (inferred); single-family code → 1 unit (derived)
1. zoning_raw = zonecode; parcel_id = 37119 + parcelnum; valuation_usd = bldgcost; final_date = compldate (completion); floor_area_sqft = heatsqft

**Known limitations**

- A 'legacy' file: the county moved residential applications to Accela in 2025 and publishes those permits in a separate Accela file, not loaded; the towns' legacy permits still run to 2026-10
- Countywide new one-unit homes are 0.88-1.02 of BPS 37119 in 2012-2022 (1.2-1.3 in 2010-2011); apartments vary 0.5-1.6 by year (permit timing)
- Code 101 is SFD unless the description names a townhouse; the county codes townhouses 102
- Permits filed under Charlotte but standing in a town after 2023-06-01 are not downloaded

### Met Council Regional Parcel Dataset, parcel points (7-county metro, 2021-2025 and current)

- **Source id:** `metc_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `states.mn.metc_parcels` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=9cea9e4cbfec4e21ac552750072dd0d5
- **Version:** 2026-10-19, roll_2021, roll_2022, roll_2023, roll_2024, roll_2025
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19
- **Files:** 3496 (3,097.3 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (Minnesota Government Data Practices Act); MetroGIS counties share parcel data without fee or license
- **Required attribution:** Metropolitan Council / MetroGIS; parcel data from Anoka, Carver, Dakota, Hennepin, Ramsey, Scott and Washington counties

**Cleaning steps**

1. 7-county parcel point layers Parcel_Points_2023, Parcel_Points_Aggregate, Parcel_Points_2021, Parcel_Points_2022, Parcel_Points_2024, Parcel_Points_2025 (https://arcgis.metc.state.mn.us/data1/rest/services/parcels), downloaded per county and OBJECTID range, requesting only OBJECTID, COUNTY_PIN, CO_CODE, CO_NAME, CTU_NAME, HOMESTEAD, ACRES_POLY, ACRES_DEED, EMV_LAND, EMV_BLDG, USECLASS1, DWELL_TYPE, FIN_SQ_FT, YEAR_BUILT, NUM_UNITS, SALE_DATE, SALE_VALUE, EXP_DATE and the point (WGS84). Owner, taxpayer and situs address fields are never requested
1. vintage = the year in the service name (current roll: year of its export); vintage_date = the county's latest EXP_DATE in that roll (the 2025 roll is a mid-2025 export)
1. parcel_id = county GEOID (CO_CODE) + COUNTY_PIN (letters and digits only); a PIN repeated within a county and roll keeps its first row
1. jurisdiction_geoid by lotline.geo.place_or_township on the point (TIGERweb ACS 2025), kept if in the MN jurisdictions table; else the jurisdiction CTU_NAME names; else the county's remainder row
1. Held-out rows removed right after jurisdictions are assigned, before attributes are read (V5-MN-STPAUL, snapshot rule: St. Paul only from rolls exported before 2024-01-01), on both the point's jurisdiction and the CTU_NAME jurisdiction
1. land_use_std: USECLASS1 by the ordered rules in config/crosswalks/mn_land_use.csv; a residential result is overridden by DWELL_TYPE rules (config/crosswalks/mn_land_use_dwelling.csv); rules flagged refine_by_units use NUM_UNITS where known (1 SF_DETACHED, 2 DUPLEX, 3-4 TRI_QUAD, 5+ MULTIFAMILY_5P); land_use_raw = USECLASS1
1. units = NUM_UNITS; null where the county leaves it unpopulated in a roll (no positive value at all, e.g. Hennepin, where it is 0 everywhere)
1. lot_sqft = ACRES_POLY × 43,560, else ACRES_DEED × 43,560, else null
1. year_built = YEAR_BUILT from 1800 to the roll year + 1, else null; bldg_sqft = FIN_SQ_FT > 0
1. land_value / bldg_value = EMV_LAND / EMV_BLDG (estimated market value, value_basis=market)
1. last_sale_price / last_sale_date = SALE_VALUE (> 0) / SALE_DATE; sale_multi_parcel = the same sale date and price on more than one parcel of the county in the roll; null for sales dated the 1st of a month (Hennepin records most sales by month only)
1. homestead: HOMESTEAD Yes/Partial → True, No → False, else null

**Known limitations**

- Rolls before 2021 are token-locked (2002-2020 services); requested from Met Council (#11)
- Hennepin leaves NUM_UNITS and DWELL_TYPE blank: units are null and land use comes from the use class only
- Use-class labels differ by county and over time; the crosswalk is rule-based (first match wins) and class 4b(1) '1-3 units' is read as 2-3 units (DUPLEX) unless units or dwelling type say otherwise
- Condominium points carry their building lot's acres, so lot_sqft overstates condo lots
- Values are the assessor's estimated market value for the roll's assessment year, not sale prices
- sale_multi_parcel can also flag separate sales at the same price on the same day (new townhomes); it is null for most Hennepin sales (month-only dates)
- Jurisdictions use 2025 boundaries; annexations since a roll's date are not reflected
- St. Paul parcels exist only in the 2021-2023 rolls (V5 holdout)

### Metropolitan Council Residential Building Permits (7-county metro)

- **Source id:** `metc_residential_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.mn.metc_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://gisdata.mn.gov/dataset/us-mn-state-metc-econ-residential-building-permts
- **Version:** 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 59 (28.3 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, Minn. Stat. ch. 13)
- **Required attribution:** Metropolitan Council, via the Minnesota Geospatial Commons

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download the 'Residential Permits' feature layer (https://arcgis.metc.state.mn.us/data1/rest/services/structure/Other_Structure_Public/FeatureServer/0) with the ArcGIS pager, requesting only OBJECTID, SDE_ID, CO_CODE, CTU_CODE, CTU_NAME, YEAR, TENURE, HOUSING_TYPE, RES_PERMIT_TYPE, BUILDINGS, UNITS, PIN, PERMIT_VALUE; address, ZIP, building/owner name and notes are never requested
1. HOUSING_TYPE SFD/ADU/TH/DTQ/MF5 → building_type_std of the same code, type_confidence=high (the survey records the type); anything else → UNKNOWN. DTQ and MF5 are never split
1. RES_PERMIT_TYPE gains (NU, MI, MU, FC, FS, FD, FM) → units_new=UNITS, units_removed=0; losses (RM, MO, TF, TC, TS, TD, TM) → units_new=0, units_removed=UNITS; RE (remodel over $1M) → both 0. Each row is one side of a ledger, so the other side is 0 by construction; a missing UNITS leaves both null
1. is_demolition=True for RM; is_conversion=True for the conversion codes (MU, TF, FC, TC, FS, TS, FD, TD, FM, TM); unknown codes leave both null
1. YEAR → issue_year; issue_date null; date_precision=year
1. jurisdiction_geoid: '27' + CTU_CODE (FIPS place code) when that place is in the MN jurisdictions table, else '27' + CO_CODE + CTU_CODE (county subdivision, e.g. townships)
1. parcel_id: '27' + CO_CODE + local PIN (punctuation removed; a leading county code stripped when the remainder has the county's local length; '0' placeholders → null)
1. permit_id: 'metc-' + SDE_ID (the layer's unique identifier)
1. Remove held-out place-years (validation/holdout.py) before the table is written

**Known limitations**

- Year of permit only, no dates; no permit number (SDE_ID is Met Council's row id, not a city's)
- City-reported annual survey; non-responding communities are filled from Census BPS without PINs
- PIN present on well under half the rows, and almost none in 2010-2014
- DTQ lumps 2-4 unit buildings; 5-6 unit buildings sit in MF5 with large buildings
- ADU recording starts in 2016 (C32): no ADU rows 2009-2013 and one in 2014 (fetch of 2026-10-14). Minneapolis ADUs 2016-2022 are about half the city's published count, so ADUs may also sit in SFD
- About 1.7% of rows are in county subdivisions not in the jurisdictions table (Carver and Scott townships, Empire, Credit River, Fort Snelling, Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community)
- Covers the 7-county metro only

### NC OneMap statewide parcels (NC1Map_Parcels; county tax data transformed by NC CGIA)

- **Source id:** `onemap_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `states.nc.onemap_parcels` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.nconemap.gov/pages/parcels
- **Version:** 2026-10-19, 2026-10-20, 2026-10-21
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21
- **Files:** 2146 (1,536.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** NC OneMap public data; county-sourced, provided as is with no warranty (no open license stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude owner names and types, mailing and site addresses, legal descriptions, subdivision names and deed references (no personal data or free text)
1. Downloaded one county at a time from the parcel-point layer (server-side filter cntyfips='<fips>', split into OBJECTID ranges); counties listed in config/crosswalks/nc_land_use_counties.csv
1. parcel_id = county GEOID + parno; a parno repeated within a county keeps the lowest OBJECTID; parcels without a parno are dropped
1. land_use_std from the county's crosswalk (config/crosswalks/nc_land_use_<county>.csv), reading the fields in the county's order; a residential land use (not a building-type field) with no building (improvval, or structyear for Union, 0) → VACANT_RESIDENTIAL where the county flag says so; unmatched → UNKNOWN
1. land_use_raw = '<field>=<code>' of the matched code (else the first field's raw value)
1. year_built = structyear when 1700..vintage year; 0 and empty → unknown
1. lot_sqft = gisacres × 43,560 (GIS polygon area); land_value/bldg_value = landval/improvval, value_basis 'assessed'; last_sale_date = saledate (before 1900 or after the roll date → unknown)
1. zoning_raw from the county's zoning field where it sends one (Durham: parusecode)
1. vintage_date = the county's transform date from NC1Map_Parcels_Transform_Dates; vintage = its year
1. jurisdiction_geoid = incorporated place by lotline.geo.place_or_township (TIGERweb ACS 2025), kept even when the place is not a BPS permit issuer; else the county remainder (5-digit GEOID)
1. Places with under half of their 2020 housing units in the loaded counties are left out (they fall back to ACS): e.g. Chapel Hill, Burlington, Clayton, Angier
1. Holdout filter with snapshot=True: the 2026 roll drops every Charlotte (3712000) parcel and, under D-012, every unincorporated Mecklenburg (37119) parcel

**Known limitations**

- Current roll only: no history; per-county transform dates differ (2026-01-07 Mecklenburg to 2026-05-29 Cabarrus on 2026-10-19)
- 48 of 100 counties: the ten largest (2020 Census) crosswalked by hand, 38 more drafted from their code inventories by keyword rules (onemap_codes) and reviewed; 46 send no usable land-use code (37 send none) and 6 were left out after a check against ACS one-unit homes (reports/nc/onemap_county_check.md); those 52 stay on the ACS fallback
- Land-use codes are county-native and crosswalked county by county; some codes are ambiguous (Mecklenburg DUPLEX-TRIPLEX → DUPLEX; patio homes → SF_ATTACHED; Wake ONE FAMILY includes townhouses and condominium units, which only the county file's Design Style separates)
- No dwelling-unit counts or building area in the layer
- structyear is empty (0) for Durham, Forsyth, Buncombe and Cabarrus; Cabarrus sends no land-use code (tier 3); Union's RES lumps every housing type; Guilford MULTI-FAMILY<4 (2-4 units) → TRI_QUAD
- Jurisdictions come from parcel points and 2025 boundaries; a place that is not a BPS permit issuer (Charlotte and the Mecklenburg towns, which BPS reports under the county) keeps its place GEOID
- Charlotte and unincorporated Mecklenburg parcels are all held out (current roll, V5 holdout, D-012): only the six Mecklenburg towns remain; a pre-2023-06-01 roll is needed for Charlotte

### OMB core-based statistical area (CBSA) delineation, July 2023 (county to metro/micro area)

- **Source id:** `census_cbsa_delineation` → table `jurisdictions (cbsa_code, cbsa_type)` (adapter `national.cbsa` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/demo/metro-micro/delineation-files.html
- **Version:** 2023; publisher files last modified up to 2023-08-04
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 1 (0.1 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Skip the title rows; keep CBSA code, title, metro/micro type and county FIPS
1. County GEOID = state FIPS + county FIPS; one CBSA per county
1. Each jurisdiction gets its county's CBSA (multi-county places: the county BPS files them under)

**Known limitations**

- Rural counties belong to no CBSA (no code)
- 2023 delineation applied to all years; CBSA boundaries changed in 2013 and 2023

### Ohio Statewide Parcels, public view (Ohio OGRIP; county auditor exports)

- **Source id:** `oh_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `states.oh.oh_parcels` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://services2.arcgis.com/MlJ0G8iWUyC7jAmu/arcgis/rest/services/OhioStatewidePacels_full_view/FeatureServer/0
- **Version:** 2026-10-19, 2026-10-26; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-26
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-27
- **Files:** 9348 (3,283.2 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Butler County public GIS data (maps.bcohio.gov; no reuse terms stated); Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office public GIS data (no reuse terms stated); Franklin County Auditor public records (disclaimer: 'as is'; no reuse terms stated); Lucas County Auditor (AREIS) public GIS data (no reuse terms stated); Montgomery County Auditor GIS downloads (no reuse terms stated); State of Ohio OGRIP public data, provided 'as is' (no use restrictions stated for public downloads); Summit County Fiscal Office public GIS data (ArcGIS Online, owner Summit_Admin; no reuse terms stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude situs and mailing address fields and CAMA links (no personal data)
1. Downloaded one county at a time (all 88) with a server-side filter (County='<name>') and OBJECTID ranges
1. Rows without a LocalParcelID (polygons with no auditor record) are dropped; parcel_id = county GEOID + LocalParcelID; a parcel ID repeated within a county (stacked polygons) keeps one row, the largest polygon
1. land_use_std from StateLUC via config/crosswalks/oh_dte_luc.csv (DTE land-use classes; 5x1-5x5 residential codes are the 5x0 use on unplatted acreage); county 'Custom Code' classes outside that pattern, 7xx abatement codes, 999 and blanks → UNKNOWN
1. lot_sqft = LandArea (acres) × 43,560 where LandArea > 0, else Shape__Area (sq ft in EPSG:3735, Ohio South State Plane)
1. vintage_date = the county's latest CurrentTo (export date); vintage = its year; a county with no CurrentTo on any parcel takes the download (snapshot) date
1. county_geoid from the county name via config/crosswalks/oh_county_fips.csv
1. County layers (COUNTY_LAYERS: Summit Fiscal Office as of 2025-03-25, Lucas Auditor tax year 2025, Cuyahoga Fiscal Office tax year 2026, Butler CURRENTPARCELS read 2026-10-26; owner and address fields never requested) joined on the parcel ID, attributes only: the county's DTE land-use code fills land_use_std where the statewide layer is UNKNOWN (never replacing a known code); residential year built → year_built (1700 to now, else unknown); a parcel listed more than once keeps its first code and its earliest year built (Summit lists each parcel twice; Franklin's Dwelling.xlsx, appraisal snapshot 2026-10-15, has one row per dwelling card and adds year built only)
1. Franklin County yearly rolls: the Auditor's Parcel.xlsx (parcel ID, LUC) from the last appraisal snapshot of 2016-2025 (except the statewide roll's year) added as vintages for jurisdictions with >= 99% of their single-family houses in Franklin County; each parcel takes the statewide roll's jurisdiction, lot size, year built and centroid, else its taxing district's jurisdiction (>= 95% of the district in one jurisdiction) with unknown lot size, else it is dropped
1. One roll per jurisdiction: after placement, a jurisdiction spanning counties with different export dates takes the latest one for all its parcels (8 jurisdictions on 2026-10-26, e.g. Twinsburg)
1. Each parcel's label point (centroid, WGS84) is requested from the server (geometry='centroid') and stored as lon/lat
1. jurisdiction_geoid by lotline.geo.place_or_township (TIGERweb ACS 2025 incorporated places, else county subdivisions), kept only if in the OH jurisdictions table; else the parcel's county subdivision if in the table; else the county's remainder row (5-digit GEOID)
1. Holdout filter applied with snapshot=True (Ohio has no holdouts)

**Known limitations**

- Jurisdictions come from centroids and 2025 boundaries, not from the auditor: a parcel straddling a boundary goes wherever its label point falls, and annexations after 2025 are not reflected
- In Franklin and Hamilton no township is a permit issuer in the jurisdictions table (the county building department permits unincorporated land), so township parcels go to the county's remainder row (174,159 parcels on 2026-10-18), as do 9 villages outside the Census permit universe (8,679: Indian Hill, Amberley); 6 parcels had no centroid polygon match
- Attributes are minimal: no units, year built, building area, values or sales; county layers fill land use and year built only where listed in COUNTY_LAYERS (Summit, Lucas, Cuyahoga, Butler, Franklin); Montgomery (Dayton) publishes no parcel land-use code: its engineer's server failed TLS verification and the Auditor's weekly geodatabase (read 2026-10-26) has only generalized land-use polygons and a building tax class
- Lucas and Cuyahoga county GIS hosts dropped connections from some networks on 2026-10-26 (they answered over a VPN); a failed county download stops the run rather than silently skipping
- A county layer is of its own date (Summit 2025-03), not the statewide export's: a parcel created after it keeps the statewide (unknown) land use
- County exports are of different dates (Franklin 2023-09-26, Hamilton 2023-08-02); the layer is a current snapshot, not a history (Franklin County's yearly Auditor files are the exception)
- Franklin yearly rolls cover only places wholly in Franklin County: Columbus (97.7% of its houses), Dublin, Westerville, Reynoldsburg, Canal Winchester and others reaching into other counties keep one roll and D-035's scaled history; parcels created after 2023 are placed by taxing district, and 50-280 eligible parcels a year with no dominant district are dropped
- Franklin's LandArea is empty or 0 for 97.5% of parcels, so its lot sizes are GIS polygon areas
- Shape__Area is in the Ohio South State Plane projection; for northern counties (Ohio North zone) the area carries a small projection error
- A parcel ID can repeat within a county (Hamilton 1,992, Franklin 15 on 2026-10-15: multi-polygon parcels); one row is kept, so a polygon-area lot size can miss the other parts
- 'Custom Code' classes (e.g. 553 in Franklin, 508 in Hamilton) vary by county and stay UNKNOWN; county crosswalks from each auditor's code list would recover them

### Ramsey County attributed parcel points (current roll, outside St. Paul)

- **Source id:** `ramsey_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `states.mn.ramsey_parcels` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.ramseycounty.us/your-government/open-government/research-data
- **Version:** 2026-10-19
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19
- **Files:** 45 (47.9 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public data (Ramsey County GIS open data; no license terms stated, Minn. Stat. ch. 13)
- **Required attribution:** Ramsey County GIS

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download https://gis.ramseycountymn.gov/server/rest/services/Cadastral/CAD_AttributedParcelPoint_ViewOnly/FeatureServer/0 with the ArcGIS pager into a dated snapshot, where SiteCityName <> 'SAINT PAUL' / SiteCityName IS NULL (two queries; parcels whose site city is St. Paul are never downloaded), requesting only OBJECTID, ParcelID, RollType, SiteCityName, HomesteadYN, ParcelAcresPolygon, ParcelAcresDeed, ParcelFrontage, EMVYear, EMVLand, EMVBuilding, LandUseCode, LandUseCodeDescription, DwellingType, LivingUnit, LivingAreaSquareFeet, YearBuilt, LastSaleDate, SalePrice, PropertyDataJoinDate and the point (WGS84). Owner, taxpayer and homestead names and addresses and the site address are never requested
1. vintage_date = latest PropertyDataJoinDate (the roll's property-data date); vintage = its year
1. parcel_id = '27123' + ParcelID (letters and digits only)
1. jurisdiction_geoid by lotline.geo.place_or_township on the point, kept if in the MN jurisdictions table; else the jurisdiction SiteCityName names; else the county
1. Held-out rows removed right after jurisdictions are assigned (V5 snapshot rule: a 2026 roll has no St. Paul rows), on both the point's jurisdiction and the site city's
1. land_use_std from LandUseCodeDescription by config/crosswalks/mn_land_use_ramsey.csv, refined by LivingUnit for flagged rules; land_use_raw = LandUseCode: LandUseCodeDescription
1. units = LivingUnit; lot_sqft = ParcelAcresPolygon (else ParcelAcresDeed) × 43,560; lot_width_ft = ParcelFrontage (> 0); year_built 1800 to the roll year + 1; bldg_sqft = LivingAreaSquareFeet (> 0)
1. land_value / bldg_value = EMVLand / EMVBuilding (estimated market value, value_basis=market)
1. last_sale_price / last_sale_date = SalePrice (> 0) / LastSaleDate; sale_multi_parcel = the same sale date and price on more than one parcel (null for sales dated the 1st of a month)
1. homestead: HomesteadYN Y/P → True, N → False

**Known limitations**

- Current roll only: no history, and no St. Paul rows (V5 holdout); St. Paul parcels through 2023 come from metc_parcels
- Frontage is missing on many parcels (irregular and interior lots)
- Values are the assessor's estimated market value for the EMV year, not sale prices
- sale_multi_parcel can also flag separate sales at the same price on the same day

### Travis Central Appraisal District certified appraisal roll (City of Austin parcels)

- **Source id:** `tcad` → table `parcels` (adapter `manual_export` v1)
- **Source:** https://traviscad.org/publicinformation/
- **Version:** 2026-07-18
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-19
- **Files:** 1 (557.2 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public information posted by Travis Central Appraisal District
- **Required attribution:** Travis Central Appraisal District

**Cleaning steps**

1. Zips are downloaded by hand in a browser (the site's bot check blocks scripted downloads) and registered with `lotline manifest register --source tcad`; nothing is fetched by script
1. Fixed-width files read by position (TCAD Legacy 8.0.33 layout): PROP.TXT, PROP_ENT.TXT, STATE_CD.TXT, LAND_DET.TXT, IMP_DET.TXT. Excluded entirely (never sliced from the record): owner names and IDs, owner, mailing and mortgage-company addresses, mortgage loan numbers, deed book/page/number, agents, ARB, lawsuit and exemption-applicant data, situs address
1. Real property only (prop_type_cd R); one row per prop_id and roll, the highest supplement
1. City placement: properties taxed by an entity named in config/crosswalks/tx_tcad_entities.csv (CITY OF AUSTIN → 4805000); others are left out
1. land_use_std: improvement (else land) state code → state category (STATE_CD.TXT ptd_state_cd) → config/crosswalks/tx_ptad_land_use.csv; land_use_raw keeps the district code
1. lot_sqft: sum of land-segment square feet, else legal acreage × 43,560
1. year_built: earliest improvement-detail year built (1800 to the roll year); units, bldg_sqft null
1. land_value / bldg_value: homestead + non-homestead appraisal values; value_basis appraisal; homestead from hs_exempt
1. parcel_id: '48453' + geo_id digits (matches the permits' tcad_id)
1. Holdout filter applied with the parcel-roll snapshot rule (Texas has no holdouts)

**Known limitations**

- Texas is a non-disclosure state: no sale prices; values are appraisals
- Units per parcel and building area are not in the export
- Land use at the state-category level only until TCAD's district subcodes are crosswalked: category A (SF_DETACHED) may include townhomes and condominiums; category B (2+ units) is OTHER
- Parcels in Austin outside Travis County (Williamson, Hays) are in other districts' rolls
- The entity-name match and the implied-decimal rule have only been tested on synthetic fixtures

### TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels (statewide, from Texas appraisal districts)

- **Source id:** `stratmap_parcels` → table `parcels` (adapter `manual_export` v1)
- **Source:** https://data.geographic.texas.gov/collection/?c=1d33dafb-6e9c-40ac-887d-f4577909ed9b
- **Version:** 2019-03, 2022-07, 2024-02, 2025-06, 2026-09
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-27
- **Files:** 5 (12,689.4 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC0 1.0 (TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Downloaded by hand in a browser (the DataHub host blocks scripts) and registered with `lotline manifest register --source stratmap_parcels`; nothing is fetched by script
1. Only parcel ID, county, tax year, land-use codes, areas, values and year built are decoded (from the .dbf or the geodatabase table); owner names, mailing and site addresses and legal descriptions are never decoded
1. land_use_std from the PTAD state code (stat_land_use) via config/crosswalks/tx_ptad_land_use.csv; blank or unmatched -> UNKNOWN
1. lot_sqft from legal_area, else gis_area, in their stated units, else the polygon's true area (equal-area projection, or Web Mercator corrected for latitude)
1. jurisdiction_geoid = incorporated place holding the polygon centroid (lotline.geo), else the county remainder; parcel_id = county GEOID + prop_id; one row per parcel and roll (largest polygon)
1. value_basis = appraisal; no sale prices (Texas non-disclosure)
1. Rolls read: 2019-03 and 2025-06 (ROLLS), each release one roll at its release year; a county part with under 80% of the county's parcels in the other release (min_county_roll_completeness) is left out with every jurisdiction that touches it

**Known limitations**

- Attribute coverage varies by appraisal district: some counties send no state land-use code or year built; the D-017 gate keeps those on the ACS denominator
- The 2026-09 release has no land-use codes and no area units for any county (all null), so its rolls never pass the land-use gate; earlier releases carry the state code for part of the state
- PTAD category B (multifamily) does not say how many units; no unit counts
- Centroids of very irregular parcels can fall just outside them; placing by centroid can misplace parcels on a city boundary

### Wake County real estate rolls, final pre-revaluation files (November 2019, December 2023)

- **Source id:** `wake_realestate` → table `parcels` (adapter `manual_export` v1)
- **Source:** https://www.wake.gov/departments-government/tax-administration/data-files-statistics-and-reports/real-estate-property-data-files
- **Version:** 2019-11-30, 2023-12-31, 2026-10-21
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-21
- **Files:** 3 (354.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Wake County public records (no license stated)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Files downloaded by hand in a browser (services.wake.gov/robots.txt disallows automated access) and registered with `lotline manifest register --source wake_realestate`; nothing is fetched by script
1. Only non-personal columns are read (USECOLS): owner names, mailing and street addresses, legal description, property index, deed book/page, special write-in and billing class are never loaded
1. Column names checked against the county Record Layout (2019-01-14): all 87 match, without 'Unused'
1. One row per card collapsed to one per parcel: card 01 gives Type & Use, Design Style, year built; units and heated area summed over cards; values, acreage, sale, zoning, city repeat on every card
1. parcel_id = 37183 + REAL_ESTATE_ID
1. land_use_std via config/crosswalks/nc_land_use_wake_realestate.csv: Type & Use + Design Style, then Type & Use, then Land Class; a residential Land Class with no building value → VACANT_RESIDENTIAL
1. year_built = Year_Built of card 01 when 1700..the roll year; 0 → unknown
1. lot_sqft = Deeded_Acreage × 43,560; land/bldg values assessed (2020 revaluation)
1. last_sale_price/date = Total_sale_Price/Total_Sale_Date (price 0 → unknown); sale_qualified = flag A or C; sale_multi_parcel = flag C; no flag → unknown
1. jurisdiction_geoid from CITY via config/crosswalks/nc_land_use_wake_jurisdictions.csv; outside city limits → 37183 (county remainder); cities mostly outside Wake (Durham, Angier, Clayton: use_wake_roll False, under 10% of 2020 housing units in Wake) are left out
1. vintage_date 2023-12-31 (Dec 2023 roll) and 2019-11-30 (Nov 2019 roll, when registered); holdout filter applied with snapshot=True (no Wake holdout)

**Known limitations**

- One county only (Wake); values are as of the preceding revaluation (2016 for the 2019 roll, 2020 for the 2023 roll), not market values in the roll year
- Jurisdiction is the assessor's city code (no coordinates); parcels in Raleigh's ETJ outside city limits go to the county remainder
- Design Style on card 01 only; multi-card parcels (1.1% of cards) take the main building's type
- Last sale only, not a sales history; the 24-month qualified-sales file (raw only) has no canonical table yet
